About the Role
Uber’s Incident Command and Cyber Resilience team, part of the Threat Defense and Response (TDR) organization, leads the response to our highest-severity cybersecurity incidents and continuously tests our ability to detect, respond to, and recover from threats. We protect Uber’s people, products, infrastructure, and data across the intersection of the digital and physical world.
We are looking for an experienced engineering manager to lead a global team and own the strategy, roadmap, and execution across Incident Command, Purple Team, the Insider Threat Program, and Cyber Resilience. You will establish clear command during critical incidents, bring the right teams together, and drive decisions that reduce harm and restore secure operations.
Your responsibility extends beyond the incident itself. You will turn lessons from real events, adversary emulation, and continuous testing into stronger detections, more effective response, and demonstrated readiness. You will also guide engineering investments in automation and AI that improve response speed and quality while preserving human judgment and accountability.
This role requires a leader who can make sound decisions with incomplete information, communicate clearly under pressure, and develop people who do the same.
What the Candidate Will Do
Lead Incident Command. Manage and develop a global team of incident commanders responsible for Uber’s highest-severity cybersecurity incidents, including active threats, critical vulnerabilities, insider risks, and security incidents involving large-scale fraud. Serve as a senior escalation point and assume command when needed.
Drive decisions and coordinated execution. Establish incident objectives, roles, priorities, escalation paths, and operating cadence. Coordinate investigation, containment, remediation, and recovery across Security, Infrastructure, Product, and Business teams, resolving dependencies and driving actions to completion.
Lead sensitive incident coordination and communication. Partner with Legal, Privacy, People, Communications, and other stakeholders to navigate complex incidents. Give executives clear assessments of impact, uncertainty, response options, and decisions required.
Own the Cyber Resilience program. Establish continuous testing and validation of detection and response capabilities across people, processes, and technology. Test the full path from adversary activity through telemetry, detection, triage, escalation, containment, and recovery.
Lead Purple Team. Set priorities for collaborative adversary emulation and testing with offensive security, threat intelligence, detection engineering, and response teams. Use realistic attack scenarios to expose gaps, drive improvements, and retest to verify that fixes work.
Own the Insider Threat Program. Define the program’s strategy, operating model, and roadmap with Security, Legal, Privacy, and People partners. Strengthen prevention, detection, investigation, and response to insider risks, with disciplined handling of sensitive information and respect for employee privacy.
Build organizational readiness. Own tabletop exercises, incident simulations, premortems, and post-incident reviews. Translate internal lessons, external incidents, and emerging threats into prioritized improvements with clear owners and verified outcomes.
Guide engineering, automation, and AI investments. Lead the development and integration of tools that improve incident coordination, evidence synthesis, decision support, and readiness testing. Define clear approval boundaries, auditability, and human oversight for consequential actions.
Set direction and measure results. Own the team’s roadmap, staffing, and delivery commitments. Establish measures for command readiness, detection and response effectiveness, validated threat coverage, and closure of recurring gaps. Integrate security response and production incident management practices to improve execution across Uber.
Build and grow the team. Hire, coach, and develop incident commanders and engineers. Set clear expectations for performance and technical quality, support career growth, and build an inclusive culture grounded in accountability, sound judgment, and continuous learning.
Basic Qualifications
8+ years of experience in security incident response, security engineering, production incident management, or security and infrastructure operations.
Experience directly managing technical teams, including hiring, performance management, career development, and delivery accountability.
Experience serving as incident commander or incident lead for high-severity cybersecurity or production incidents in complex, distributed environments.

About the Role
Uber is launching AV Labs to accelerate the autonomous technology ecosystem. We're building out a high-velocity team of multi-disciplinary experts to turn real-world operations into high-quality data for our autonomous partners. This team is focused on the hardest problem in AV today: unlocking real-world, long-tail driving data. Autonomy is now a data race—and Uber has an edge: We collect rare, real-world driving data at a scale and capital efficiency no one else can match.
Our AV Labs Hardware team is pioneering the next-generation E/E architecture for our cutting-edge L4 data collectioncapable vehicle fleet.You will drive critical projects ranging from initial 3rd-party hardware driver and firmware development to the embedded development, bring-up, and deployment of our in-house designed production hardware. As a Senior Embedded Engineer, your technical expertise will directly accelerate our path to production, playing a key role in shaping the reliability of our autonomous data collection fleet.
What the Candidate Will Do
Develop Core Firmware & Drivers: Design, write, and maintain robust firmware and low-level device drivers for 3rd-party automotive-grade components and critical AV sensors (LiDAR, radar, cameras) to enable immediate, high-fidelity data collection and shadow mode operations.
Drive In-House Hardware Bring-Up: Execute the transition to production by taking ownership of board bring-up, hardware validation, and low-level software deployment for our custom, in-house designed autonomous computing platforms.
Collaborate on HW/SW Co-Design: Partner closely with electrical and hardware engineering teams to implement hardware-software interfaces, participate in schematic reviews, and ensure component selection aligns with firmware requirements.
Debug & Optimize Complex Systems: Utilize hardware debugging tools (oscilloscopes, logic analyzers) and software profiling to troubleshoot intricate system-level issues, optimize sensor data pipelines, and ensure strict timing and network synchronization across the vehicle.
Contribute to Team Excellence: Act as a technical resource and mentor within the hardware team, actively contributing to best practices for embedded software architecture, code quality, and scalable deployment.
Basic Qualifications
Embedded Software Experience: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, accompanied by 7+ years of professional experience developing embedded software using modern C/C++ in RTOS (e.g., FreeRTOS, Embedded Linux) or bare-metal environments.
Low-Level Driver & Automotive Hardware Expertise: Strong experience writing firmware and device drivers for complex, automotive-grade components, SoCs, and autonomous vehicle sensors (e.g., LiDAR, radar, cameras). This must include hands-on experience with sensor integration, board bring-up, hardware debugging tools (e.g., oscilloscopes, logic analyzers), and familiarity with standard automotive interfaces and vehicle networks (e.g., CAN/CAN-FD, Automotive Ethernet, FPD-Link/GMSL, PCIe, SPI, I2C).
Production Lifecycle Execution: Demonstrated experience contributing to embedded hardware systems from initial prototyping and 3rd-party integration through to production deployment—ideally within the autonomous vehicle, robotics, or mission-critical automotive domains.
Preferred Qualifications
Hardware-Software Co-Design: Experience collaborating closely with electrical and hardware engineers on custom board designs, including participation in schematic reviews and component selection for computing platforms.
Functional Safety & Automotive Standards: Understanding of automotive functional safety standards and their application in embedded software development, including experience with ISO 26262 (ASIL B through ASIL D) compliance and adherence to coding guidelines like MISRA C/C++.
Advanced Timing & Synchronization: Experience with distributed system timing and hardware synchronization methodologies critical for sensor fusion. Familiarity with Precision Time Protocol (PTP/gPTP, IEEE 802.1AS) and hardware PPS routing across complex vehicle networks is highly valued.
High-Performance AV Compute Platforms: Experience developing firmware and drivers for modern, high-performance autonomous driving SoCs and compute platforms (e.g., NVIDIA DRIVE, Qualcomm Snapdragon Ride) and optimizing data pipelines utilizing hardware accelerators (GPUs, DSPs, NPUs).

uber-303285.text:
About the role
We are building the next generation of fleet infrastructure that determines how millions of vehicles come onto and operate on Uber's platform.
Uber's fleet foundations today are mobility-centric and assume a human driver operating a single vehicle. Autonomous fleets have no driver. Delivery fleets carry materially different fulfillment semantics. Fleets increasingly operate across more than one Uber marketplace at the same time. The foundational abstractions that served a single line of business no longer hold, and the work of unifying them has to be done against a live global fleet estate that cannot be interrupted.
This is a highly platform-focused team, addressing challenges that range from modelling physical-world supply into marketplace systems, to building the partner-facing integration surface through which external fleet operators onboard, to evolving foundational domain models beneath systems carrying live production traffic without disrupting the operating business.
What the Candidate Will Do:
Lead the architecture, strategy and multi-year technical roadmap for Uber's fleet foundations across mobility, delivery and autonomous use cases
Define unified fleet and earner abstractions spanning human-driver, delivery and autonomous fleets, and drive their adoption across Uber's Earner, Identity, Fulfillment, Pricing, Marketplace and Matching platforms
Drive cross-team and cross-functional alignment across multiple Line of Business and platform teams, targeting fleet onboarding time, launch velocity and partner integration cost
Own architectural coherence between Uber's fleet entity model and the fulfillment semantics of autonomous and delivery use cases as those use cases are incorporated into shared foundations
Lead the evolution of Uber's third-party fleet integration surface so that autonomous, delivery and mobility fleet operators onboard through the same foundations, and so that partner integrations move from bespoke engineering to self-serve configuration
Own backward compatibility and migration safety for Uber's existing global fleet estate throughout the transition, across jurisdictions with differing licensing, insurance and tax treatment
Engage deeply with engineers across the marketplace platform organizations to identify gaps, streamline workflows and define long-term platform solutions
Act as a technical partner to EMs, PMs and staff engineers, contributing to org-wide and company-wide fleet and autonomous strategy
Provide hands-on technical direction, mentoring and design leadership to senior and staff engineers across fleet and platform teams
Influence global fleet platform initiatives and ensure strong collaboration across sites, time zones and partner organizations
About the Team:
Fleet & Vehicle Platform systems sit on the critical path for every vehicle and every fleet-operated earner that wants to transact on the platform. If we don't succeed, a vehicle cannot be onboarded, a fleet operator cannot bring supply online, and an autonomous or delivery fleet cannot be introduced to Uber's marketplace at all. Our work is driven by the physical realities of vehicle fleets — ownership, operators, shifts, bases, licensing, insurance and jurisdiction — modelled into a marketplace that was originally built for individual drivers operating single vehicles. We build and maintain a sophisticated stack that includes:
Fleet and Vehicle Identity and Onboarding: Representing fleets, fleet operators and fleet-affiliated earners as first-class entities, onboarded by a third party rather than by Uber.
Fleet Entity and Lifecycle Modelling: The foundational domain model and state machines describing how a fleet, its vehicles and its earners exist and change over time across the marketplace.
Third-Party Fleet Operator Integration: The external API surface and integration platform through which independent fleet operators, dispatch software vendors and autonomous partners connect their supply to Uber.
Fleet Supply Semantics in Matching and Fulfillment: Multi-vehicle earner association, shift-based availability, base and home-location semantics, fleet-level acceptance behaviour and street-hail eligibility within Uber's matching and fulfillment systems.
Fleet Economics: Fleet-specific fees, surcharges, commission structures and jurisdictional tax treatment expressed within Uber's pricing and billing systems.
Fleet Configuration and Self-Serve Operations: The configuration platform enabling fleet capabilities to be launched, varied by market and operated without bespoke engineering per partner.
Fleet Monitoring, Incident Management and Maintenance: Deployment, monitoring, intelligence, incident handling and maintenance workflows for vehicles and fleets in operation.
Autonomous and Delivery Fleet Foundations: Extending all of the above to fleets with no human driver, and to fleets whose fulfillment semantics differ materially from mobility.
Furthermore, we collaborate with platform teams across Uber — Vehicle, Earner, Identity, Marketplace, Fulfillment, Pricing, Safety, Delivery and Autonomous Mobility — to ensure fleet capabilities serve every Uber line of business through one set of foundations rather than many.
Basic qualifications:
PhD or equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics or related field AND 4-years full-time Software Engineering work experience OR 7-years full-time Software Engineering work experience, WHICH INCLUDES 4-years total technical software engineering experience in one or more of the following areas:
Programming language (e.g. C, C++, Java, Python, or Go)
Note the 4-years total of specialized software engineering experience may have been gained through education and full-time work experience, additional training, coursework, research, or similar (OR some combination of these). The years of specialized experience are not necessarily in addition to the years of Education & full-time work experience indicated.
Technical skills:
Required:
Deep hands-on experience building and operating distributed backend systems at scale.
3+ years of hands-on experience modelling vehicles, fleets, operators, couriers or other physical-world supply as first-class entities in a large-scale marketplace or logistics platform, together with experience in at least one of:
Evolving foundational domain models under live production traffic, or owning platform capabilities across more than one marketplace or line of business.
Demonstrated ownership of multi-year, cross-organizational platform programs with heavy dependencies across many partner teams, including driving alignment and influencing technical direction outside of direct reporting lines.
Demonstrated experience designing and owning external API surfaces and partner-facing integration platforms through which third-party operators connect that physical-world supply
Preferred:
Experience with autonomous vehicle, connected-vehicle or EV ecosystems, adjacent to the domain areas above.
Experience with delivery, logistics or last-mile fulfillment platforms, adjacent to the domain areas above.
Experience with pricing, fares, commission or billing systems, including jurisdictional variation, adjacent to the domain areas above.
Experience working with external partners, enterprise customers or regulated counterparties, adjacent to the domain areas above.

Uber has evolved from a ride-hailing service into an all-in-one platform, connecting users globally through various on-demand offerings across UberX and UberEats. About the Role
Our mission is to protect, defend, and secure Uber's products, infrastructure, and data by building highly available, scalable, and extensible security solutions and services. We focus on proactively identifying and mitigating security risks, strengthening foundational security controls, and continuously evolving our defenses to stay ahead of emerging threats.
We are seeking an experienced Senior Staff Security Engineer, Enterprise Security to provide technical leadership in architecting, building, and scaling security capabilities that protect Uber's enterprise environment. This role will drive the evolution of our security architecture and platforms across corporate endpoints, infrastructure, enterprise applications, and cloud environments.
As Uber's technology footprint grows and the threat landscape evolves, traditional approaches to enterprise security must give way to scalable, automated, and security-by-default solutions. You will lead complex, cross-organizational initiatives to modernize foundational security controls, reduce attack surfaces, improve threat prevention and detection capabilities, and strengthen cyber resilience.
What You Will Do
Define and drive the technical strategy, architecture, and roadmap for Enterprise Security, aligning security investments with evolving threats, business priorities, and Uber's technology landscape.
Architect and lead the implementation of security solutions across corporate endpoints, production infrastructure, and enterprise environments, applying defense-in-depth and zero-trust security principles.
Drive technical advancements in endpoint protection, endpoint detection and response (EDR), application control, system hardening, security posture management, and infrastructure security across macOS, Windows, and Linux environments.
Design and scale security capabilities to protect enterprise applications and corporate data, including secure access, browser security, SaaS security, data exfiltration prevention, and application-level security enforcement.
Architect and build scalable security platforms, services, and automated workflows that improve security coverage, reduce operational complexity, and enable consistent enforcement of security controls.
Partner with Infrastructure, IT, Client Platform Engineering, Cloud Security, and other engineering teams to drive security-by-default architecture, resolve complex technical challenges, and deliver security improvements at scale.
Establish high standards for security engineering, architectural design, software quality, and operational excellence. Influence technical decisions, and raise the engineering bar across the organization.
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience in Computer Science, Engineering, Cybersecurity, or a related technical field.
10+ years of professional experience in security engineering, systems engineering, infrastructure security, or software engineering, with significant experience designing and implementing security solutions at scale.
Deep technical expertise in one or more enterprise security domains, such as endpoint security, infrastructure security, EDR, application control, zero-trust architecture, or enterprise security platforms.
Strong understanding of operating system security, networking, authentication, authorization, and security architecture across macOS, Windows, and Linux environments.
Proficiency in one or more programming languages such as Golang, Python, Java, or C/C++, with demonstrated experience building production-grade software, automation, or security infrastructure.
Demonstrated experience leading complex, large-scale technical initiatives, making architectural decisions, and influencing engineering teams beyond immediate organizational boundaries.
Preferred Qualifications

Deep expertise in enterprise endpoint and infrastructure security technologies, including EDR/XDR, device management, system hardening, and endpoint security controls.
Experience designing and deploying security solutions across large-scale environments spanning corporate devices, on-premises infrastructure, and public cloud platforms.
Strong understanding of enterprise security technologies such as Secure Access Service Edge (SASE), Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA), secure enterprise browsers, SaaS security, and data loss prevention.
Experience architecting highly available, fault-tolerant security services, including safe deployment strategies, observability, failure recovery, and operational resilience.
Experience applying AI/ML, agentic systems, or advanced automation to security operations, threat analysis, security policy enforcement, or incident investigation.

About the role and team
At Uber, machine learning powers some of the most complex real-time decisions in the world — from matching riders with drivers and optimizing marketplace efficiency to personalizing experiences across Mobility and Delivery.
We are making a significant investment in the next generation of machine learning, with a particular focus on building large-scale Foundation Models trained on Uber's proprietary marketplace data.
Unlike general-purpose large language models trained primarily on text and code, our foundation models will learn from rich, heterogeneous sequences of real-world interactions across Uber's ecosystem. These models have the potential to fundamentally transform how we understand and predict marketplace behavior, improve existing ML systems, and unlock entirely new capabilities.
We are looking for an exceptional Principal Engineer, Machine Learning / AI to help lead this effort.
This is a highly strategic, hands-on technical leadership role with the opportunity to shape Uber's foundation model architecture, influence ML investments, and work across multiple engineering and product organizations. You will help establish deep technical expertise in large-scale model development and accelerate foundation model initiatives across Uber.
Uber’s engineering team executes on the vision and builds the products for the future of urban mobility: deeply understanding our customers to solve their transportation needs with innovative technology. Engineering leaders at Uber move lightning fast to build, test, learn, and iterate, working in small teams that control their own destiny and own their own critical metrics. Leadership helps the vision become a reality and clears obstacles out of the way. Some of the brightest data scientists, designers, engineers, and marketers in the industry are here to build amazing products on top of leading-edge platforms for data, machine learning, and experimentation.
The products we build are used by millions of riders, drivers, eaters, restaurants, and others to earn money for their families, and get around faster, easier, cheaper, and with less environmental impact.
What you’ll do
Architect and build large-scale Foundation Models: Lead the technical design, development, and training of large sequence-based Transformer models using Uber's proprietary marketplace data.
Define the technical direction: Help shape Uber's long-term foundation model strategy, including model architectures, training approaches, representation learning, and scaling.
Advance representation learning: Develop powerful embeddings and learned representations that can improve downstream ML models across recommendations, ranking, personalization, marketplace optimization, and other applications.
Drive company-wide ML impact: Partner with engineering and ML teams across Mobility, Delivery, Earner, Merchant, and Consumer experiences to accelerate the adoption and impact of foundation models.
Build scalable ML capabilities: Influence the development of training infrastructure, distributed computing capabilities, and efficient approaches for training and deploying large models.
Provide deep technical leadership: Solve complex modeling challenges, guide architectural decisions, and establish technical best practices for large-scale model development.
Collaborate across organizations: Work closely with senior technical leaders, researchers, and engineering teams to align initiatives, share expertise, and drive innovation.
Remain hands-on : Contribute directly to critical technical decisions, model development, experimentation, and complex engineering challenges while providing Principal-level leadership.
Basic Qualifications
BS degree in Computer Science or related technical field, or equivalent experience.
A minimum of 10 years of relevant software engineering experience, with a proven record of technical leadership and innovation.
Extensive experience designing, building, and scaling deep learning systems and large-scale AI infrastructure.
Preferred Qualifications
Masters/PhD in Computer Science or related technical field.
Direct hands-on experience building, training, or scaling large Foundation Models, particularly sequence-based Transformers.
Deep expertise in large-scale AI/ML infrastructure, model training systems, and distributed computing.
Strong understanding of modern deep learning techniques, including pretraining, representation learning, embeddings, and sequence modeling.
Strong software engineering and system design skills.
Demonstrated ability to independently lead complex technical initiatives, balancing hands-on technical contributions with long-term architectural thinking and cross-organizational influence.

The Team
The security organization at Uber is dedicated to enabling safe and secure innovation while protecting the communities we serve both online and in the physical world. Our team is responsible for protecting both people and their data across intersections of the digital and physical world. The primary objective for Uber's Engineering Security team is to enable the technical ambitions of the company while maintaining the highest standards of security and privacy for our customers and partners. As cybersecurity threats evolve, so do we.
Detection Engineering sits at the center of that mission. We own the end-to-end path from raw security telemetry to a high-fidelity, actionable case in a responder's hands — the detection content, the platforms that run it, and the signal quality our incident responders depend on. We ingest and normalize telemetry from every control plane at Uber — endpoint (EDR), identity, network, cloud, and AI-agent activity — and turn it into detections that fire fast enough and clean enough to matter.
About the Role
Our mission is to protect, defend, and secure Uber's products, infrastructure, and data by building highly available, scalable, and extensible security solutions and services. We are focused on proactively identifying and remediating security risks as well as swiftly detecting and mitigating security incidents. In the ever-evolving landscape of cybersecurity, we continuously adapt and evolve our defenses in order to always stay one step ahead of potential threats.
We are seeking a talented and experienced Senior Manager to lead our Detection Engineering organization and own the strategy, roadmap, and execution for how Uber detects adversary activity at global scale. You will be accountable for detection coverage against a prioritized threat model, for the latency and fidelity of every signal we produce, and for the engineering platforms that make detection development a fast, testable, measurable discipline rather than an artisanal one.
This is a role for a leader who is as comfortable debating ATT&CK coverage gaps and false-positive economics with a staff detection engineer as they are setting a multi-half roadmap with Security Response, Threat Intelligence, Infrastructure, and Product partners. The security landscape is constantly evolving, and with the adoption of ML/GenAI backed by extensive heterogeneous data, both the threat surface and our detection toolkit are expanding rapidly. With your deep expertise across detection, response, and large-scale data systems, you will lead major efforts to design, implement, and scale industry-leading detection capabilities. You are not only a role model, but also an empathetic leader - a humble teacher who grows engineers and managers while delivering uniquely challenging projects.
What the Candidate Will Do
In this role you will define and execute the strategic roadmap for threat detection across Uber's corporate, production, and cloud environments. The scope includes:
Detection strategy and coverage. Own a versioned, prioritized threat-scenario inventory (grounded in MITRE ATT&CK, intelligence-driven priorities, and newly emerging surfaces) and be accountable for provable detection coverage per scenario and environment, not anecdotal coverage claims.
Detection content and detection-as-code. Lead the teams that author, test, tune, and retire detection logic across SIEM rules, batch/warehouse detections, behavioral and anomaly models, correlation logic, and vendor-native signals. Establish lifecycle standards: every detection has an owner, a mapped use case, test coverage, a documented response path, and measured performance.
Detection platform and pipeline. Set direction for the ingestion, normalization, enrichment, and alerting infrastructure that detections run on - streaming and batch - including end-to-end observability of source freshness, completeness, mapping errors, and enrichment failures.
Latency and fidelity as hard goals. Drive measurable, time-bound improvements in time-to-detect for the highest-priority scenarios, and in signal-to-noise for the response queue. Recover responder capacity by eliminating low-value alerting without degrading true-positive rate.
AI/ML for cyber defense. Lead the responsible adoption of ML and LLM-based techniques for detection, triage, correlation, and case enrichment — moving them from research to production with fairness, safety, auditability, and compliance built into the engineering practice.
Partner with response. Operate in tight feedback loop with Security Response & Investigations, Threat Intelligence, and the SOC so detection quality is measured by investigative outcomes, not rule counts. Act as a senior escalation point during high-severity events and drive detection gaps surfaced in post-incident review back into the roadmap.
Cross-functional influence. Collaborate with Infrastructure, Corporate IT, Identity, Product Engineering, Legal, and Privacy to secure telemetry access, land instrumentation at the source, and integrate detection into systems and development lifecycles across Uber.
Build and lead the team. Manage a team of highly skilled security and software engineers — including senior/staff ICs and, over time, managers and tech leads — fostering a culture of technical excellence, operational rigor, continuous improvement, and strong customer focus. Set clear, ambitious goals to hire, develop, and retain a diverse and inclusive team, and deliver against them.
Vendor and build/buy strategy. Evaluate, select, and manage relationships with external security vendors and platforms; make and defend complex build-vs-buy and cost-vs-coverage tradeoffs with a clear view of short- and long-term implications.
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Security, or a related technical field.
5+ years of full-time work experience in software engineering or security engineering prior to Engineering Management experience.
5+ years of full-time Engineering Management experience, including experience leading senior/staff engineers and growing other leaders (managers and/or tech leads).
Demonstrable domain expertise owning complex detection and response programs: threat detection, detection engineering, SIEM/security analytics, incident response, or security data platforms at enterprise or cloud scale.
Proven track record of setting multi-team technical strategy and delivering against it over multiple planning cycles, with measurable outcomes in coverage, time-to-detect, or alert quality.
Ability to make complex decisions with incomplete information in ambiguous situations and environments, and to hold accountability for those decisions.
Great interpersonal skills, deep technical ability, and a track record of successful execution in security engineering or software development at cloud scale.
Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to convey detection strategy, systemic risk, and tradeoffs to both executive leadership and senior engineers.
Preferred Qualifications
Master's Degree or PhD in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Security, or a related field.
Hands-on background in detection engineering: authoring and tuning detection logic across log, network, endpoint, identity, and cloud telemetry, with a track record of improving coverage and signal fidelity while reducing false-positive burden on responders.
Experience operating a modern detection stack at scale — SIEM/security data lake (e.g., Elastic, Splunk), streaming pipelines (e.g., Kafka, Flink), warehouse-based batch detections, EDR (e.g., CrowdStrike, SentinelOne), CNAPP/CDR (e.g., Wiz), identity providers (e.g., Okta), and SOAR/case management (e.g., Torq).
Experience with public cloud security across multiple providers (GCP, OCI, AWS) and modern containerized/orchestrated environments.
Experience incorporating AI/ML and LLM-based techniques into production security systems, including evaluation methodology and precision/recall management.
Experience partnering with EMs, TPMs, and PMs on prioritization, headcount planning, and technical evaluation of team members.
Experience leading teams across multiple locations and working across multiple in-house engineering organizations.
Familiarity with relevant industry frameworks and compliance mandates (e.g., MITRE ATT&CK, NIST CSF, ISO 27001, SOC 2).

About the Role
Uber is launching AV Labs to accelerate the autonomous technology ecosystem. We're building out a high-velocity team of multi-disciplinary experts to turn real-world operations into high-quality data for our autonomous partners. This team is focused on the hardest problem in AV today: unlocking real-world, long-tail driving data. Autonomy is now a data race—and Uber has an edge: We collect rare, real-world driving data at a scale and capital efficiency no one else can match.
Our AV Labs Hardware team is building the next-generation E/E architecture for our L4 data-collection vehicle fleet. The automotive MCU beside the main compute platform owns what must always work: vehicle network access, power sequencing, thermal and voltage supervision, time synchronization, and secure firmware updates. You will own that firmware from third-party board support through bring-up and deployment of our in-house production hardware.
What the Candidate Will Do
Core firmware and drivers: Design, write and maintain C firmware and drivers for automotive MCUs (Infineon AURIX TriCore) on FreeRTOS and AUTOSAR Classic: CAN-FD, Ethernet, SPI, I2C, LIN, ADC, PWM and on-board devices such as switches, PMICs and IMUs.
Vehicle I/O: Own the bridge between vehicle CAN-FD buses and the compute SoC, including buffering, filtering, timestamping and latency.
Power, thermal and time: Implement power sequencing, sleep and wake, voltage and temperature monitoring, fan control, SoC watchdog and reset supervision, and gPTP and PPS time distribution.
Bootloader and secure update: Own the bootloader and dual-bank (A/B) update path, including versioning, signing, rollback and recovery of field units.
Bring-up and co-design: Own board bring-up and validation for custom hardware. Join schematic reviews with hardware engineers, and debug with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers and on-chip debuggers such as Lauterbach TRACE32.
Supplier code and releases: Integrate and regression-test supplier firmware drops, keep builds automated and reproducible, and mentor teammates on code quality and best practices.
Basic Qualifications
Embedded experience: Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or a related field, with 7+ years developing embedded software in C/C++ on an RTOS or bare metal.
Automotive MCU expertise: Hands-on firmware and driver work on automotive-grade MCUs (AURIX TC3xx preferred; Renesas RH850, NXP S32 or similar considered), with CAN/CAN-FD and Ethernet, board bring-up, and hardware debugging tools.
Production lifecycle: Experience taking embedded systems from prototype and third-party integration to production, ideally in autonomous vehicle, robotics or mission-critical automotive domains.
Preferred Qualifications
Security: Hardware security module (HSM) and secure boot experience, including secure update, key management and chain of trust on automotive MCUs.
AURIX and AUTOSAR: AURIX iLLD and AUTOSAR Classic (MCAL and BSW configuration with tools such as Vector or ETAS).
Functional safety: ISO 26262 (ASIL B through D) and MISRA C, including safety mechanisms such as watchdogs, memory protection and E2E.
Timing: PTP/gPTP (IEEE 802.1AS) and hardware PPS routing across vehicle networks.
AV compute platforms: MCU-to-SoC interfaces on autonomous driving platforms such as NVIDIA DRIVE or Jetson.

About the Role
Uber is launching AV Labs to accelerate the autonomous technology ecosystem. We're building out a high-velocity team of multi-disciplinary experts to turn real-world operations into high-quality data for our autonomous partners. Autonomy is now a data race—and Uber has an edge: We collect rare, real-world driving data at a scale and capital efficiency no one else can match.
Our AV Labs Hardware team is building the next-generation E/E architecture for our L4 data-collection vehicle fleet. A fleet only collects useful data when its compute, MCU and sensors work reliably in the car, and when a fault can be found and fixed without a technician on site. You will build the diagnostics, monitoring and dashboards that make fleet health visible, from MCU and SoC firmware to fleet dashboards, and you will bring our hardware to life in vehicles and support the path to production-line testing.
What the Candidate Will Do
Diagnostics and fault management: Design and implement fault detection, event and DTC handling, UDS and DoIP services, and watchdog supervision across the MCU and the Linux compute platform.
Monitoring framework: Design and own the vehicle health monitoring pipeline: collect metrics, logs and fault events from the MCU (CAN, serial or UDP) and the Linux SoC, and send them to a central time-series and log store using standard tooling (for example Prometheus exporters or OpenTelemetry collectors).
Deep system observability: Use eBPF and kernel tracing to observe Linux SoC behavior with low overhead: scheduling, network, driver and camera pipeline latency, and frame or packet drops.
Dashboards and alerting: Build dashboards (for example in Grafana) for fleet, vehicle and board health: temperatures, voltages, power state, bus load, time sync offset, camera link status and update status. Define alert rules and thresholds, and route alerts to on-call.
Vehicle bring-up and integration: Commission the compute, MCU and sensor stack in vehicles (CAN-FD, Ethernet, power sequencing, GNSS, IMU, cameras) and validate gPTP and PPS timing.
Field triage and test automation: Use monitoring data to reproduce and root-cause vehicle issues with the reliability and software teams, and turn each one into an automated regression test and, where useful, a new dashboard panel or alert.
Safety and security of diagnostics: Contribute to safety analysis (FMEA, FMEDA) and implement safety mechanisms. Protect diagnostic access with authenticated sessions and security access.
Production line support: Define the diagnostic interfaces and readouts (unit identity, firmware versions, pass or fail data) that end-of-line test stations use, with the manufacturing test team.
Basic Qualifications
Embedded experience: Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or a related field, with 7+ years developing embedded software in C/C++ on an RTOS, embedded Linux or bare metal.
Automotive diagnostics: Hands-on experience with UDS (ISO 14229), DTC handling and ISO-TP over CAN; DoIP (ISO 13400) is a plus.
Vehicle networks and integration: Strong experience with CAN/CAN-FD and Automotive Ethernet, tools such as Vector CANoe or similar, oscilloscopes and logic analyzers, and integrating compute platforms and sensors in vehicles.
Linux observability: Hands-on experience debugging system-level issues on embedded Linux with eBPF-based tools and profilers (for example bpftrace, bcc or perf).
Monitoring and visualization: Experience building monitoring for devices or fleets (for example with Prometheus and Grafana): instrumentation or exporters, dashboards and alert rules, in Python, Go or C/C++.
Production lifecycle: Experience taking embedded systems from prototype and third-party integration to production, ideally in autonomous vehicle, robotics or mission-critical automotive domains.
Preferred Qualifications
Observability stack: Experience with log and time-series stacks (for example Loki, ELK, OpenTelemetry, InfluxDB), eBPF-based observability tools, and fleet-scale telemetry pipelines (retention, cardinality, cost).
Security: Hardware security module (HSM) and secure boot experience, plus secure diagnostics (UDS security access, authenticated sessions, key management).
AUTOSAR diagnostics: Configuring Dcm, Dem, FiM, WdgM and E2E modules in an AUTOSAR Classic stack.
Functional safety: ISO 26262 (ASIL B through D), ASPICE and MISRA C/C++.
Production and service tooling: End-of-line test, factory programming or remote service diagnostics tooling.
Linux and AV compute: Linux kernel, device tree and Yocto board support, and experience with platforms such as NVIDIA DRIVE or Jetson.

About the role and team
Uber’s Security Engineering team’s mission is to protect, defend, and secure Uber’s products, infrastructure and data by building highly available, scalable and extensible security solutions and services. We are focused on proactively identifying and remediating security risks as well as swiftly detecting and mitigating security incidents. In the ever-evolving landscape of cybersecurity, we continuously adapt and evolve our defenses in order to always stay one step ahead of potential threats.
As a passionate and pragmatic technologist, you will lead efforts within the organization to drive the development and operations of security services and frameworks to support user-facing products and platforms across Uber. At Uber, Principal Engineers are among the top 2% of our engineering community—senior technologists who combine vision with execution. They are trusted experts who design at scale, write production-quality code, mentor senior engineers, and set the technical culture across teams.
In this role, you will be the Principal Engineer for Uber's security foundation: the identity and trust layer that every other system depends on. Thousands of services, tens of thousands of employees and partners, and a rapidly growing population of AI agents must each prove who they are and what they are permitted to do — on every request, in every region. You will own the multi-year technical direction for that foundation across our identity-first, Zero Trust stack: workload identity and service-to-service authentication, human and non-human identity, PKI and cryptographic trust, authorization policy, secrets, and device trust. You will set this direction as Uber moves rapidly toward an agentic future, where autonomous agents become first-class actors that must be identified, authorized, attributed, and contained with the same rigor we apply to humans and services, and as the company expands into new business verticals that each bring new trust boundaries, regulators, and partners.
What you’ll do
Technical Roadmap & Vision: Define and deliver the multi-year architecture and strategy for Uber's identity-first Zero Trust stack, translating company-wide goals into organization, team, and project-level technical direction across multiple engineering organizations.
Engineer at Core: Design, prototype, and ship secure systems. Stay hands-on in the hardest problems — the architecture you set is one you can build, review, and debug.
Engineering Excellence: Set and hold the technical bar across the security foundation organization through design review, architectural standards, and written technical direction. Elevate the performance of engineers across organizations through mentorship and sponsorship of staff-and-above ICs.
Reliability of Tier-0 Trust Infrastructure: Identity, policy decision, and certificate services sit in the critical path of production traffic; their failure is a company-wide failure. Own availability, failure-mode, and blast-radius design for these systems, convert incident learnings into architectural fixes, and govern the safe rollout of enforcement changes.
Identity for the Agentic Era: Extend the identity and authorization plane to AI agents as first-class principals — agent identity and attestation, delegated authorization and token exchange for agent-to-agent and agent-to-service traffic, risk-adaptive control over agent actions, and runtime attribution of every agent action back to an accountable human or service owner.
Drive Fleet-Wide Adoption: Lead cross-organization migrations that retire legacy trust primitives — static secrets, long-lived credentials, implicit network trust — in favor of short-lived, attested identity, and see them through to measurable fleet coverage under strict availability constraints.
Enable New Business Verticals: Ensure the identity foundation extends cleanly to new business lines, acquisitions, cloud estates, and SaaS and partner boundaries, with a consistent model for non-human identity and least privilege.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with infrastructure, AI platform, product engineering, and business teams to integrate security seamlessly, and represent the identity and Zero Trust strategy to executive stakeholders. Influence, not authority, is the instrument.

BS Degree in Computer Science or related field.
10+ years of experience in software engineering,with deep specialization in cybersecurity.
Proven track record as a technical leader—driving design, influencing architecture, and mentoring senior engineers across organizational boundaries
Expert knowledge in one or more of: identity and access management, zero trust architecture, secure systems design, applied cryptography, authorization and policy systems, or agentic/AI security
Hands-on experience owning highly available, Tier-1 distributed systems in the critical path of production traffic — design, operation, and incident response
Strong coding skills in languages such as Go, Python, Java, C++, or Rust
Experience building scalable, reliable, and secure infrastructure at large scale
Preferred Qualifications
Advanced degree (Master’s or PhD) in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
Experience designing or operating Zero Trust architectures at scale: SPIFFE/SPIRE or equivalent workload identity, service mesh authentication, centralized policy decision services, device trust, and secretless service-to-service authentication.
Depth in authentication and authorization protocols: OAuth 2.0/OIDC, SAML, SCIM, mutual TLS, and PKI/certificate lifecycle management.
Experience securing AI/agentic systems — agent identity, delegated authorization, guardrails, sandbox isolation, or runtime attribution for autonomous workloads.
Experience with non-human identity at scale: service accounts, API keys, cloud IAM hardening, and credential lifecycle across multi-cloud and SaaS estates.
Experience leading large-scale credential or authorization migrations across a heterogeneous fleet.
Contributions to open standards or the external security community (specifications, talks, publications, open source).
Advanced degree in Computer Science or a related field.

About the role and team
Uber's Marketplace Matching team builds the real-time decision systems that determine how riders and drivers are matched across a global, two-sided marketplace. These decisions happen under uncertainty, at massive scale, and with competing short- and long-term objectives across marketplace efficiency, reliability, sustainable growth, user value, and quality of experience.
We are looking for a Staff Machine Learning Engineer to help define and build the next generation of matching optimization systems. This role sits at the intersection of machine learning, sequential decision-making, optimization, control, and marketplace dynamics. You will own major optimization charters, set technical direction, and lead ambiguous 0→1 problems from formulation through large-scale production deployment. The work is highly applied: new ideas and novel methods are strongly valued, but the goal is not research for its own sake. Success means finding the best solution — whether invented, adapted from state of the art, or significantly improved — and making it work reliably in a complex real-world marketplace
What you’ll do
Set technical direction and own major charters for Uber's real-time matching optimization and ML systems.
Design matching objectives and decision policies that balance multiple competing marketplace goals across riders, drivers, and the platform.
Develop and productionize ML-based decision systems for complex sequential and multi-agent environments.
Apply techniques from reinforcement learning, probabilistic modeling, deep learning, causal inference, and sequential decision-making to large-scale marketplace problems.
Explore model predictive control and other feedback-control approaches for dynamically adapting matching behavior as marketplace conditions evolve.
Build behavioral models that capture rider and driver responses to marketplace decisions and incorporate those responses into optimization.
Develop simulation, experimentation, and causal measurement frameworks to evaluate policies and understand long-term system effects.
Lead ambiguous 0→1 technical efforts, from problem formulation and modeling through production inference and system integration.
Identify opportunities where new algorithms or modeling approaches can materially improve marketplace performance, while pragmatically adapting proven techniques when they are the better solution.
Work closely with engineering, applied science, economics, product, and operations teams to translate complex marketplace problems into scalable technical solutions.
Mentor senior engineers and raise the technical bar for ML and optimization across the broader matching organization.
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience.
8+ years of industry experience in machine learning, or 6+ years with a PhD or equivalent demonstrated technical depth.
Significant experience building large-scale production ML systems, including online inference.
Deep expertise in modern machine learning, including deep learning, reinforcement learning and the principles underlying decision-making under uncertainty.
Demonstrated ability to formulate ambiguous business or system problems as tractable ML or decision problems and drive them from concept to production. Strong BE programming and systems skills, with the ability to personally design and implement production-quality ML and optimization systems.
Experience leading technically complex, cross-functional initiatives and influencing engineering or scientific direction beyond an individual project.
Preferred Qualifications
PhD in Machine Learning, Reinforcement Learning, Control, Optimization, Robotics, Operations Research, Statistics, or a closely related field.
Deep experience with reinforcement learning, optimal control, or related sequential decision-making methods.
Background in large-scale decision systems such as (two-sided) marketplace optimization, robotics/autonomy, ads optimization, ranking, or recommendation systems.
Strong understanding of marketplace economics, incentives, behavioral responses, and the dynamics of two-sided platforms.
Experience designing multi-objective or multi-agent decision systems with complex interactions and long-term effects.
Experience with causal inference and rigorous online or offline evaluation of ML-driven policies.
Experience with large-scale simulation environments for policy development and evaluation.
Track record of introducing novel modeling or algorithmic approaches that materially improved a production system.

About the Role
Uber has expanded its services beyond transporting people to include the delivery of nearly anything customers need, often within hours , with Grocery & Retail being a major growth priority.
The Grocery and Retail Consumer Ranking Team is dedicated to creating a seamless and efficient shopping experience, enabling users to effortlessly find what they need.
As the Engineering Manager for the Grocery & Retail Consumer Ranking team, you will lead the evolution of Uber’s online ranking architecture and high-throughput serving stack. We are looking for a systems-focused leader to drive the design of our online retrieval and ranking services. This role is at the intersection of complex distributed systems and product innovation, requiring a leader who can balance rapid experimentation with rock-solid operational excellence.

Own the Roadmap: Define, prioritize, and execute an ambitious product roadmap through strong people leadership—managing, coaching, and growing all team members.
Drive Reliability & Performance: Lead high-impact initiatives to improve p99 latency, tail-latency mitigation, and infra-cost efficiency for high-QPS services.

Technical Vision: Lay out the multi-quarter roadmap for ranking infra, leveraging senior ICs to drive architectural migrations and capacity planning.

Operational Ownership: Proven track record in managing SLOs/SLAs, incident response, and performance/latency optimization.

---- Preferred Qualifications ----

Optimization: Proven ability to make practical tradeoffs among latency, model quality, capacity, and maintainability.
Project Impact: History of leading multi-quarter re-architecture projects or migrations that significantly reduced costs or improved availability.

The Team
The security organization at Uber is dedicated to enabling safe and secure innovation while protecting the communities we serve both online and in the physical world. Our team is responsible for protecting both people and their data across intersections of the digital and physical world. The primary objective for Uber’s Engineering Security team is to enable the technical ambitions of the company while maintaining the highest standards of security and privacy for our customers and partners. As cybersecurity threats evolve, so do we.
About the Role:
Our mission is to protect, defend, and secure Uber’s products, global infrastructure, and data by building highly available, scalable, and extensible network security solutions and services. We are focused on proactively architecting resilient network boundaries, building next-generation edge security controls, and mitigating threats such as DDoS and automated bot attacks at massive global scale.
We are seeking a talented and experienced Sr. Staff Security Engineer to join our Cyber Defense team. With your deep technical expertise across large-scale distributed systems, edge architectures, zero-trust network design, and threat mitigation technologies, you will lead major initiatives to design, implement, and scale industry leading network security solutions. You are not only a visionary technical leader, but also an empathetic mentor who elevates engineering teams while delivering solutions to uniquely challenging problems. You will collaborate closely with cross-functional infrastructure, security, and product engineering teams to shape our global network security strategy.
What you will do:
Lead the overall technical vision, architecture, and long-term strategy for Uber’s global network security capabilities, including Secure Access Service Edge (SASE), Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA), network segmentation, perimeter defense, bot detection/mitigation, and volumetric DDoS protection.
Architect, implement, and scale high-performance, distributed backend systems and edge services to defend against advanced network threats in real-time.
Evaluate, select, integrate, and manage relationships with external security vendors and third-party platforms to enhance threat coverage, edge mitigation, and challenge capabilities.
Establish network security engineering standards, conduct comprehensive architectural reviews, and ensure end-to-end resilience and low latency across global infrastructure.
Collaborate across organizational boundaries to seamlessly integrate network security into global systems and development lifecycles.
Lead critical network security incident response and mitigation efforts during high-severity threat events, performing thorough post-incident analysis to drive systematic prevention.
Mentor, guide, and sponsor engineers across the organization, fostering a culture of technical excellence, innovation, and continuous growth.
Communicate complex network security concepts, systemic risks, and strategic initiatives clearly to both executive leadership and technical teams.
Participate in security audits and compliance initiatives, providing technical expertise and ensuring adherence to security standards.
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Security, or a related technical field.
10+ years of full-time work experience in security engineering, software engineering, or network security.
Proven track record of designing, building, and scaling enterprise-grade network security solutions, backend distributed systems, or perimeter defense infrastructure.
Proficiency in at least one production programming language such as Go, Java, or C++.
Deep domain expertise in core network security concepts (e.g., L3/L4/L7 firewalls, zero-trust network access, network segmentation, DDoS mitigation, bot defense, and ingress/egress filtering).
Strong background in public cloud network security architectures (AWS, GCP, OCI) and modern containerized/orchestrated environments (Kubernetes, Docker).
Demonstrated experience leading multi-team technical projects, setting engineering strategy, and mentoring junior engineers.
Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, and architectural skills with a focus on low-latency, high-availability distributed systems.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to convey complex technical architectures and risk tradeoffs to diverse stakeholders.
Preferred Qualifications
Master’s Degree or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Security, or a related field.
Direct experience architecting and operating large-scale bot defense, edge security, SASE/ZTNA frameworks, or volumetric DDoS mitigation systems in global, high-traffic production environments.
Hands-on experience deploying AI/ML models into edge production systems for threat detection and real-time network enforcement.
Familiarity with real-time data streaming technologies (e.g., Kafka, Apache Flink) and low-latency feature stores.
In-depth experience evaluating and integrating third-party edge security vendor platforms and challenge mechanisms.
Strong understanding of relevant industry frameworks, compliance mandates, and network auditing standards (e.g., NIST CSF, ISO 27001, SOC 2).

About the role and team
Uber is launching AV Labs to accelerate the autonomous technology ecosystem. We're building out a high-velocity team of multi-disciplinary experts to turn real-world operations into high-quality data for our autonomous partners. This team is focused on the hardest problem in AV today: unlocking real-world, long-tail driving data. Autonomy is now a data race—and Uber has an edge: We collect rare, real-world driving data at a scale and capital efficiency no one else can match.
As a Principal Engineer, you will be at the forefront of Physical AI, building advanced autonomy systems and architectures to add rich semantics to our massive driving data. You will set the technical direction for the development and implementation of foundational algorithms, onboard/offboard systems, and data pipelines that enable better data mining, deep scene understanding, and causal modeling of ego vehicle behavior. You aren't just solving known problems; you are identifying the next generation of challenges in AV, designing the architectural foundations to solve them, and raising the bar for technical excellence across the entire engineering organization.
What you’ll do
Strategic Technical Vision: Lead the overarching technical strategy for AV Labs' engineering initiatives. Set the roadmap for complex algorithms, data platforms, and autonomy infrastructure that extract high-fidelity semantic meaning from urban edge cases to enrich our L4 data lake.
Architecture & System Design: Provide the overarching technical vision for managing upstream sensor dependencies, evaluating large-scale simulation frameworks, and modeling real-world behavior.
Technical Mentorship & Influence: Mentor senior, staff, and lead engineers, fostering a culture of rigorous experimentation and engineering excellence. You will serve as a technical standard-bearer and influence the architectural direction of multiple teams.
Platform Evolution: Define the requirements for high-quality large evaluation datasets, objective performance metrics, and the ultimate data mining engine that empowers autonomous partners to query and extract precise edge cases.
Cross-Organizational Leadership: Act as a critical bridge between AV Labs and other Uber engineering units to ensure our core architectures, evaluation platforms, and autonomous technologies are successfully integrated and deployed.
Basic Qualifications

About the Role
As a member of Uber’s Security Review Team, you will proactively identify and reduce risk across Uber’s most critical services and emerging technologies. You will conduct hands-on penetration testing to identify and validate real-world attack paths, perform security design reviews and threat modeling for critical services and AI agents, and partner with engineering teams to drive effective remediation.
You will also help transform how offensive security operates at scale by building AI-powered automation and security tooling that makes assessments faster, more continuous, and more comprehensive. This role combines deep technical security expertise with an automation-first engineering mindset, evolving traditional point-in-time testing toward continuous, scalable adversarial security testing across Uber’s technology ecosystem.
This position focuses on security and privacy design reviews, threat modeling, and hands-on testing of third-party AI agents. The ideal candidate is comfortable analyzing technical designs, evaluating how systems handle sensitive data, identifying potential attack paths, and translating findings into practical recommendations. You’ll work closely with engineering, security, privacy, and third-party partners to address risks while using AI-assisted workflows and automation to improve assessment quality and scale.
What You'll Do
Conduct security and privacy design reviews for services, applications, APIs, and AI integrations. Evaluate architecture, data flows, access controls, and proposed safeguards to identify risks early in development.
Perform threat modeling for critical services and AI agents, identifying attack surfaces, trust boundaries, potential attack paths, and appropriate mitigations.
Test third-party AI agents through hands-on adversarial assessments, evaluating risks across models, data access, permissions, tools, external integrations, and runtime behavior. Validate whether identified weaknesses can lead to unauthorized actions or sensitive-data exposure.
Evaluate sensitive-data handling across services and AI integrations, assessing how data is collected, accessed, stored, shared, retained, and deleted. Partner with privacy stakeholders to identify gaps and recommend appropriate safeguards.
Document actionable findings with clear descriptions, supporting evidence, reproducible test steps where applicable, risk assessments, and practical remediation guidance.
Partner with engineering teams and third-party vendors to address assessment findings, clarify security and privacy requirements, and verify that implemented mitigations resolve the identified risks.
Build and improve AI-powered automation for design reviews, threat modeling, agent testing, and vulnerability validation, reducing repetitive work and increasing assessment consistency, depth, and throughput.
Develop reusable assessment materials such as review checklists, threat models, test cases, and reporting templates to support repeatable, high-quality assessments across the team.
Basic Qualifications
3+ years of experience in security engineering, application security, product security, offensive security, or related technical security roles.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
Experience reviewing technical designs and identifying security risks in applications, APIs, cloud services, or distributed systems.
Experience performing threat modeling, analyzing attack paths, and recommending mitigations based on technical risk and potential impact.
Understanding of security and privacy principles, including authentication, authorization, least privilege, data protection, and secure handling of sensitive information.
Hands-on experience with security testing, vulnerability investigation, or validating the effectiveness of security controls.
Experience writing code or automation using languages such as Python, Go, Bash, or similar, and familiarity with AI-assisted development workflows.
Ability to communicate technical findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, document actionable recommendations, and collaborate across teams with evolving priorities.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience conducting security assessments or adversarial testing of third-party AI agents, large language model applications, or systems that interact with external tools and data sources.
Experience performing privacy design reviews and evaluating data flows, access patterns, retention practices, and safeguards for sensitive data.
Experience assessing AI-specific risks involving prompt injection, unintended data disclosure, excessive permissions, or unsafe tool use.
Experience building internal security tooling or using AI to automate design analysis, threat modeling, test execution, or assessment reporting.
Experience assessing security across interconnected cloud services, enterprise SaaS platforms, and third-party integrations.
Experience coordinating multiple assessments, working directly with engineering teams and vendors, and driving findings through remediation and validation.

About the Role
As a Senior Staff Engineer at Uber, you will serve at the highest level of technical leadership, defining strategic direction, system architecture, and technical vision across global engineering platform teams and core business units. Senior Staff Engineers at Uber exert broad influence on critical technology and business choices across various organizations. In this role, you will act as a pragmatic, passionate technologist capable of designing, building, and deploying resilient, large-scale systems. Beyond executing on uniquely complex initiatives, you will act as an accessible thought leader, collaborative partner, and humble mentor, guiding and developing talented engineering teams.
The Communications Platform at Uber powers all real-time and asynchronous customer interactions worldwide. Operating as the underlying engine for global engagement, the platform provides high-throughput, fault-tolerant, low-latency & cost efficient smart routing infrastructure across voice, SMS, chat, push notifications, email and other 3rd party messaging channels(whatsapp etc) for Riders, Drivers, Couriers, Merchants, and Enterprise partners. About the Role
Uber's Tech Risk and Assurance team, part of Engineering Security, helps Uber understand its cybersecurity risk, decide what to do about it, and prove that controls work. Our goal is to make every experience with Uber simple, secure, and safe for riders, eaters, drivers, and partners.
As a Security Technologist II, you will work on both risk and assurance projects. On the assurance side, you will test whether security controls are designed and operating effectively across Uber's systems, infrastructure, and vendors, and help automate that testing so it runs continuously. On the risk side, you will support risk assessments, maintain risk and issue records, and analyze exceptions so that leaders can see where risk sits and what has been decided.
This role suits someone who is technically fluent and likes to automate. You will read system configurations and access data, write scripts and queries to collect evidence and test controls at scale, and use AI tools to reduce manual review. Senior team members set the scope of your projects, and you will own their delivery end to end.
What You'll Do
Test the design and operating effectiveness of security controls across enterprise IT, cloud, SaaS, and third-party environments, and document clear, evidence-based findings.
Conduct control and configuration assessments to identify deviations from policy, standards, and baseline requirements, and give guidance on remediation and audit readiness.
Build and maintain automated control tests and continuous control monitoring in partnership with system owners, so that controls are tested on full populations rather than samples.
Write scripts and queries to collect and validate audit evidence, reducing manual effort for the assurance team and engineering stakeholders.
Support internal and external audits and certifications, such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, and regional regulatory assessments, including evidence requests and walkthroughs.
Track corrective actions from audits and assessments, including Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), and follow up with owners until issues are closed.
Support risk assessments of systems, applications, and vendors. Gather context, identify risks to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information systems, and draft risk statements and treatment recommendations.
Maintain risk register and issue records so that each risk has a current rating, owner, and status, and link control test results and audit findings to the risks they affect.
Review security exception requests for completeness, compensating controls, and expiry, and flag repeat or long-running exceptions for escalation.
Explore and implement AI- and LLM-based solutions, for example to classify security findings, summarize audit trails, or perform first-pass reviews of third-party security reports.
Build dashboards and reports on control test results, issue aging, and exception trends for the team and partner teams.
Recommend improvements to policies, procedures, and standards based on control testing results.
Improve runbooks and documentation for the processes you work on, and help onboard new team members.
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Information Systems, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
3+ years of experience in IT audit, security assurance, risk assessment, security issue management, or a related technical role.
Experience assessing control design and operating effectiveness across enterprise IT and cloud environments.
Technical fluency in at least one area such as identity and access management, cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, or OCI), logging and monitoring, vulnerability management, or change management, enough to read configurations and access data directly.
Hands-on automation experience, including scripting in Python or a similar language and querying data with SQL to collect evidence, test controls, or analyze results.
Experience with audit remediation tracking, risk registers, or corrective action management.
Knowledge of control frameworks and standards such as NIST CSF, NIST 800-53, ISO 27001, SOC 2, CIS, and PCI DSS.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including writing clear findings for technical and non-technical audiences.
Preferred Qualifications
Certifications such as CISA, CISSP, CRISC, Security+, or a cloud security certification.
Track record of leading IT audits, risk assessments, or control evaluations.
Knowledge of IT audit methodologies, including sampling, walkthroughs, and evidence standards.
Experience building automated control tests or continuous control monitoring.
Experience applying AI and automation to control testing, evidence collection, or findings analysis.
Experience with GRC or workflow tools such as ServiceNow eGRC, AuditBoard, Archer, or Jira.
Ability to use data to tell a clear story through a risk and assurance lens.
Strong attention to detail, an analytical mind, and strong problem-solving skills.
Why Uber?
You will see how security controls work across one of the world's largest technology platforms, and help build the automation that tests them. Working with engineering, security, audit, privacy, and compliance teams, you will turn evidence into decisions about which risks get fixed and which get accepted.
We value curiosity, thoughtful problem-solving, collaboration, and continuous learning. We welcome candidates from different backgrounds and industries and encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every qualification.

About the role and team
Engineering at Uber means building for real-world impact under real-world constraints. As a Senior Staff Backend Engineer, you will lead the architecture and implementation of next-generation distributed systems that power the bedrock of Uber. This is a high-stakes, high-impact role where you’ll tackle some of the most complex infrastructure challenges in the industry: building sub-50ms latency systems that handle 1M+ requests per second, and designing resilient platforms that power tens of billions of dollars in global marketplace transactions across 70+ countries.
This isn't just about writing code; it's about setting the technical direction for an entire organization in a fast-moving, high-ambiguity environment. You will need to move the needle for the business by building systems that are not only highly available and reliable but also developer-friendly, enabling rapid innovation across ML and Product teams. If you think in systems, stay calm under the pressure of global scale, and are motivated by the "messy" reality of solving hard problems—this is where you’ll grow.
What you’ll do
Lead the design and implementation of highly available, resilient, and cost-efficient distributed systems that serve millions of users with strict sub-50ms latency requirements.
Architect systems capable of handling 1M+ requests per second while maintaining 99.99% availability and strong consistency guarantees for critical financial and pricing flows.
Drive technical strategy for platform evolution, microservices architecture, and API design to simplify integration for new lines of business and third-party partners.
Build platform abstractions and developer tools that hide massive underlying complexity, enabling ML and product teams to iterate rapidly on core algorithms.
Spearhead architectural transitions toward "Dual-rail" resiliency, ensuring every mission-critical payment or pricing flow has redundant processing options to maximize reliability.
Partner cross-functionally with Product, Data Science, and Ops at the Director and VP levels to translate commercial requirements into scalable, hardened platform solutions.
